title: Would a much tighter stop-loss (down to -0.25%) beat the current -3% baseline? Plus a direct recovery-frequency check: how often does price recover after breaching -0.5%?

tables.name: Stop-loss/trailing-floor configs vs live baseline, tight-stop-loss extension (528 tested)

notes: User's 2026-10-03 hypothesis on return from vacation: 'a tight threshold like -0.5% would have outperformed the current -3% with actual trading, stocks rarely recover.' The 2026-09-17 profit-maximization run only tested down to -1.5%; this extends to -0.25% and adds a direct recovery-frequency analysis independent of the grid.

conclusion.summary: 0/528 configs beat the current -3%/+0.5% baseline on avg_pct on both splits, even with the stop-loss grid extended down to -5.00%. See the recovery-frequency check above for the direct answer on how often waiting past a tight stop would have paid off.
